Artist Rachel Youn creates kinetic sculptures and installations that combine artificial plants, discarded consumer objects and mechanical devices to imitate the movements of living organisms. In Pretty Behavior (2026), Youn modifies a neck massager and connects it to an artificial orchid and leaves using metal hardware, chains and glass. Once activated, the machine makes the flower shake and move continuously, giving the synthetic plant an uncanny appearance of life. Youn frequently repurposes massagers and other machines originally designed to act on the human body, redirecting their repetitive movements into artificial plants.
